shloka_text: रसातलं प्रविष्टायां वैदेह्यां सर्ववानराः । चुक्रुशुः साधु साध्वीति मुनयो रामसन्निधौ ।। 7.98.1 ।।
transliteration: rasātalaṃ praviṣṭāyāṃ vaidehyāṃ sarvavānarāḥ | cukruśuḥ sādhu sādhvīti munayo rāmasannidhau || 7.98.1 ||
translation: रसातलं into the netherworld, प्रविष्टायां having entered, वैदेह्यां when Vaidehi (Sita), सर्ववानराः all the monkeys, चुक्रुशुः cried out, साधु excellent, साध्वीति excellent (feminine), मुनयो the sages, रामसन्निधौ in the presence of Rama.
explanation: When Vaidehi entered the netherworld, all the monkeys and sages present before Rama cried out "Excellent! Excellent!"
comments: Stricken with grief and rage, Rama demands that Earth restore Sita or grant him entry, threatening her destruction -- Brahma appears, bids him not grieve, reminds him of his nature as Vishnu, and promises reunion with the pure Sita in heaven -- extolling Valmiki's poem and bidding Rama hear its remaining Uttara portion, Brahma departs, and the grieving Rama arranges for the rest to be sung on the morrow.

shloka_text: दण्डकाष्ठमवष्टभ्य बाष्पव्याकुलितेक्षणः । अवाक्छिरा दीनमना रामो ह्यासीत्सुदुःखितः ।। 7.98.2 ।।
transliteration: daṇḍakāṣṭhamavaṣṭabhya bāṣpavyākulitekṣaṇaḥ | avākchirā dīnamanā rāmo hyāsītsuduḥkhitaḥ || 7.98.2 ||
translation: दण्डकाष्ठम् a staff, अवष्टभ्य leaning upon, बाष्पव्याकुलितेक्षणः with eyes agitated by tears, अवाक्छिरा with head bowed down, दीनमना with a sorrowful mind, रामो Rama, ह्यासीत् indeed was, सुदुःखितः extremely distressed.
explanation: Leaning upon a staff, with his eyes agitated by tears, his head bowed down, and his mind filled with sorrow, Rama was indeed extremely distressed.

shloka_text: स रुदित्वा चिरं कालं बहुशो बाष्पमुत्सृजन् । क्रोधशोकसमाविष्टो रामो वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.98.3 ।।
transliteration: sa ruditvā ciraṃ kālaṃ bahuśo bāṣpamutsṛjan | krodhaśokasamāviṣṭo rāmo vacanamabravīt || 7.98.3 ||
translation: स He, रुदित्वा having wept, चिरं for a long, कालं time, बहुशो many times, बाष्पम् tears, उत्सृजन् shedding, क्रोधशोकसमाविष्टो overcome by anger and sorrow, रामो Rama, वचनम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Having wept for a long time and shedding many tears, Rama, overcome by both anger and sorrow, then spoke these words.

shloka_text: अभूतपूर्वं शोकं मे मनः स्प्रष्टुमिवेच्छति । पश्यतो मे यथा नष्टा सीता श्रीरिव रूपिणी ।। 7.98.4 ।।
transliteration: abhūtapūrvaṃ śokaṃ me manaḥ spraṣṭumivecchati | paśyato me yathā naṣṭā sītā śrīriva rūpiṇī || 7.98.4 ||
translation: अभूतपूर्वं unprecedented, शोकं sorrow, मे my, मनः mind, स्प्रष्टुम् to touch, इवेच्छति seems to desire, पश्यतो while I watched, मे my, यथा just as, नष्टा disappeared, सीता Sita, श्रीरिव like the goddess of fortune, रूपिणी embodied.
explanation: My mind seems to desire an unprecedented sorrow, as Sita, who was like the embodied goddess of fortune, disappeared right before my eyes.

shloka_text: सा ऽदर्शनं पुरा सीता लङ्कापारे महोदधेः । ततश्चापि मयानीता किं पुनर्वसुधातलात् ।। 7.98.5 ।।
transliteration: sā 'darśanaṃ purā sītā laṅkāpāre mahodadheḥ | tataścāpi mayānītā kiṃ punarvasudhātalāt || 7.98.5 ||
translation: सा That, अदर्शनं disappearance, पुरा formerly, सीता Sita, लङ्कापारे on the other side of Lanka, महोदधेः of the great ocean, ततश्चापि and from there, मयानीता brought by me, किं what, पुनर् again, वसुधातलात् from the surface of the earth.
explanation: Formerly, Sita disappeared on the other side of Lanka, beyond the great ocean, and even from there I brought her back; how much more difficult will it be to retrieve her from the surface of the earth now?

shloka_text: वसुधे देवि भवति सीता निर्यात्यतां मम । दर्शयिष्यामि वा रोषं यथा मामवगच्छसि ।। 7.98.6 ।।
transliteration: vasudhe devi bhavati sītā niryātyatāṃ mama | darśayiṣyāmi vā roṣaṃ yathā māmavagacchasi || 7.98.6 ||
translation: वसुधे O Earth, देवि O Goddess, भवति (you) are, सीता Sita, निर्यात्यतां let her be brought forth, मम to me, दर्शयिष्यामि I will show, वा or, रोषं anger, यथा so that, माम् me, अवगच्छसि you understand.
explanation: O Goddess Earth, bring forth Sita to me, or else I will show you my wrath so that you understand who I am.

shloka_text: कामं श्वश्रूर्ममैव त्वं त्वत्सकाशाद्धि मैथिली । कर्षता हलहस्तेन जनकेनोद्धृता पुरा ।। 7.98.7 ।।
transliteration: kāmaṃ śvaśrūrmamaiva tvaṃ tvatsakāśāddhi maithilī | karṣatā halahastena janakenoddhṛtā purā || 7.98.7 ||
translation: कामं indeed, श्वश्रूः mother-in-law, मम my, एव indeed, त्वं you, त्वत्सकाशात् from you, हि indeed, मैथिली Maithili (Sita), कर्षता by one who was ploughing, हलहस्तेन with a plough in hand, जनकेन by Janaka, उद्धृता was taken out, पुरा formerly.
explanation: Indeed, you are my mother-in-law, for Maithili was certainly taken out from you by Janaka, who was ploughing with a plough in hand, long ago.

shloka_text: तस्मान्निर्यात्यतां सीता विवरं वा प्रयच्छ मे । पाताले नाकपृष्ठे वा वसेयं सहितस्तया ।। 7.98.8 ।।
transliteration: tasmānniryātyatāṃ sītā vivaraṃ vā prayaccha me | pātāle nākapṛṣṭhe vā vaseyaṃ sahitastayā || 7.98.8 ||
translation: तस्मात् therefore, निर्यात्यतां let her be brought forth, सीता Sita, विवरं an opening, वा or, प्रयच्छ give, मे to me, पाताले in the netherworld, नाकपृष्ठे on the surface of heaven, वा or, वसेयं I would dwell, सहितः accompanied, तया by her.
explanation: Therefore, bring forth Sita, or grant me an opening, so that I may dwell with her either in the netherworld or on the surface of heaven.

shloka_text: आनय त्वं हि तां सीतां मत्तो ऽहं मैथिलीकृते । न मे दास्यसि चेत्सीतां यथारूपां महीतले ।। 7.98.9 ।।
transliteration: ānaya tvaṃ hi tāṃ sītāṃ matto 'haṃ maithilīkṛte | na me dāsyasi cetsītāṃ yathārūpāṃ mahītale || 7.98.9 ||
translation: आनय bring, त्वं you, हि indeed, तां her, सीतां Sita, मत्तः maddened, अहं I, मैथिलीकृते for the sake of Maithili, न not, मे to me, दास्यसि you will give, चेत् if, सीतां Sita, यथारूपां in her true form, महीतले on the surface of the earth.
explanation: You must indeed bring that Sita, as I am maddened for Maithili's sake; if you do not give Sita to me in her true form on the surface of the earth, then...

shloka_text: सपर्वतवनां कृत्स्नां विधमिष्यामि ते स्थितम् । नाशयिष्याम्यहं भूमिं सर्वमापो भवत्विह ।। 7.98.10 ।।
transliteration: saparvatavanāṃ kṛtsnāṃ vidhamiṣyāmi te sthitam | nāśayiṣyāmyahaṃ bhūmiṃ sarvamāpo bhavatviha || 7.98.10 ||
translation: सपर्वतवनां with mountains and forests, कृत्स्नां entire, विधमिष्यामि I will destroy, ते your, स्थितम् existence, नाशयिष्यामि I will destroy, अहं I, भूमिं the earth, सर्वम् everything, आपः water, भवतु let it become, इह here.
explanation: I will destroy your entire existence, including all mountains and forests, I will annihilate the earth, and let everything here become water.

shloka_text: एवं ब्रुवाणे काकुत्स्थे क्रोधशोकसमन्विते । ब्रह्मा सुरगणैः सार्धमुवाच रघुनन्दनम् ।। 7.98.11 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ bruvāṇe kākutsthe krodhaśokasamanvite | brahmā suragaṇaiḥ sārdhamuvāca raghunandanam || 7.98.11 ||
translation: एवं thus, ब्रुवाणे while speaking, काकुत्स्थे to Kakutstha (Rama), क्रोधशोकसमन्विते filled with anger and sorrow, ब्रह्मा Brahma, सुरगणैः with the hosts of gods, सार्धम् together, उवाच spoke, रघुनन्दनम् to the delight of the Raghus (Rama).
explanation: While Rama, filled with anger and sorrow, was speaking thus, Brahma, accompanied by the hosts of gods, addressed him.

shloka_text: राम राम न सन्तापं कर्तुमर्हसि सुव्रत । स्मर त्वं पूर्वकं भावं मन्त्रं चामित्रकर्शन ।। 7.98.12 ।।
transliteration: rāma rāma na santāpaṃ kartumarhasi suvrata | smara tvaṃ pūrvakaṃ bhāvaṃ mantraṃ cāmitrakarśana || 7.98.12 ||
translation: राम O Rama, राम O Rama, न not, सन्तापम् sorrow, कर्तुम् to do, अर्हसि you ought, सुव्रत O virtuous one, स्मर remember, त्वम् you, पूर्वकम् former, भावम् state (of being), मन्त्रम् sacred incantation, च and, अमित्रकर्शन O destroyer of enemies.
explanation: O virtuous Rama, you should not grieve; O destroyer of enemies, remember your ancient divine nature and the sacred incantation.

shloka_text: न खलु त्वां महाबाहो स्मारयेयमनुत्तमम् । इमं मुहूर्तं दुर्धर्ष स्मर त्वं जन्म वैष्णवम् ।। 7.98.13 ।।
transliteration: na khalu tvāṃ mahābāho smārayeyamanuttamam | imaṃ muhūrtaṃ durdharṣa smara tvaṃ janma vaiṣṇavam || 7.98.13 ||
translation: न not, खलु indeed, त्वाम् you, महाबाहो O mighty-armed one, स्मारयेयम् I would remind, अनुत्तमम् the unsurpassed (state), इमम् this, मुहूर्तम् moment, दुर्धर्ष O unconquerable one, स्मर remember, त्वम् you, जन्म birth, वैष्णवम् divine (Vishnu's).
explanation: O mighty-armed and unconquerable one, I would indeed remind you of your unsurpassed divine nature; at this very moment, remember your divine birth as Vishnu.

shloka_text: सीता हि विमला साध्वी तव पूर्वपरायणा । नागलोकं सुखं प्रायात्त्वदाश्रयतपोबलात् ।। 7.98.14 ।।
transliteration: sītā hi vimalā sādhvī tava pūrvaparāyaṇā | nāgalokaṃ sukhaṃ prāyāttvadāśrayatapobalāt || 7.98.14 ||
translation: सीता Sita, हि indeed, विमला pure, साध्वी virtuous, तव your, पूर्वपरायणा solely devoted from the beginning, नागलोकम् to the Naga world, सुखम् happily, प्रायात् went, त्वदाश्रयतपोबलात् by the strength of her penance relying on you.
explanation: Indeed, Sita, pure, virtuous, and solely devoted to you from the beginning, happily went to the Naga world by the power of her penance and devotion to you.

shloka_text: स्वर्गे ते सङ्गमो भूयो भविष्यति न संशयः । अस्यास्तु परिषन्मध्ये यद्ब्रवीमि निबोध तत् ।। 7.98.15 ।।
transliteration: svarge te saṅgamo bhūyo bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ | asyāstu pariṣanmadhye yadbravīmi nibodha tat || 7.98.15 ||
translation: स्वर्गे in heaven, ते your, सङ्गमः union, भूयः again, भविष्यति will be, न no, संशयः doubt, अस्याः of this, तु but, परिषन्मध्ये in the midst of the assembly, यत् what, ब्रवीमि I say, निबोध understand, तत् that.
explanation: There is no doubt that your union with her will happen again in heaven; but understand what I am about to tell you in the midst of this assembly.

shloka_text: एतदेव हि काव्यं ते काव्यानामुत्तमं श्रुतम् । सर्वं विस्तरतो राम व्याख्यास्यति न संशयः ।। 7.98.16 ।।
transliteration: etadeva hi kāvyaṃ te kāvyānāmuttamaṃ śrutam | sarvaṃ vistarato rāma vyākhyāsyati na saṃśayaḥ || 7.98.16 ||
translation: एतदेव this alone, हि indeed, काव्यं poem, ते by you, काव्यानाम् among poems, उत्तमं best, श्रुतम् heard. सर्वं all, विस्तरतः in detail, राम O Rama, व्याख्यास्यति will explain, न not, संशयः doubt.
explanation: This poem, which you have heard, is indeed the best among all poems, and Rama will explain everything in detail without a doubt.

shloka_text: जन्मप्रभृति ते वीर सुखदुःखोपसेवनम् । भविष्यदुत्तरं चेह सर्वं वाल्मीकिना कृतम् ।। 7.98.17 ।।
transliteration: janmaprabhṛti te vīra sukhaduḥkhopasevanam | bhaviṣyaduttaraṃ ceha sarvaṃ vālmīkinā kṛtam || 7.98.17 ||
translation: जन्मप्रभृति from birth onwards, ते your, वीर O hero, सुखदुःखोपसेवनम् experiencing joys and sorrows. भविष्यदुत्तरं and the future, च and, इह here, सर्वं all, वाल्मीकिना by Valmiki, कृतम् composed.
explanation: O hero, Valmiki has composed everything, from your birth and the experiences of joy and sorrow, to the future events that will unfold.

shloka_text: आदिकाव्यमिदं राम त्वयि सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् । नह्यन्यो ऽर्हति काव्यानां यशोभाग्राघवादृते ।। 7.98.18 ।।
transliteration: ādikāvyamidaṃ rāma tvayi sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam | nahyanyo 'rhati kāvyānāṃ yaśobhāgrāghavādṛte || 7.98.18 ||
translation: आदिकाव्यम् this first poem, इदं this, राम O Rama, त्वयि in you, सर्वं all, प्रतिष्ठितम् established. न not, हि indeed, अन्यः another, अर्हति deserves, काव्यानां among poems, यशोभाग्राघवादृते the share of glory, except for Rama.
explanation: O Rama, this primeval poem is entirely founded upon you, and indeed, no one else but you, O Raghava, deserves the glory among poems.

shloka_text: श्रुतं ते पूर्वमेतद्धि मया सर्वं सुरैः सह । दिव्यमद्भुतरूपं च सत्यवाक्यमनावृतम् ।। 7.98.19 ।।
transliteration: śrutaṃ te pūrvametaddhi mayā sarvaṃ suraiḥ saha | divyamadbhutarūpaṃ ca satyavākyamanāvṛtam || 7.98.19 ||
translation: श्रुतं heard, ते by you, पूर्वम् previously, एतत् this, हि indeed, मया by me, सर्वं all, सुरैः with gods, सह together. दिव्यम् divine, अद्भुतरूपं of wondrous form, च and, सत्यवाक्यम् truthful words, अनावृतम् unconcealed.
explanation: Indeed, I have previously heard all of this, which is divine, of wondrous form, and contains unconcealed truthful words, along with the gods.

shloka_text: स त्वं पुरुषशार्दूल धर्मेण सुसमाहितः । शेषं भविष्यं काकुत्स्थ काव्यं रामायणं शृणु ।। 7.98.20 ।।
transliteration: sa tvaṃ puruṣaśārdūla dharmeṇa susamāhitaḥ | śeṣaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ kākutstha kāvyaṃ rāmāyaṇaṃ śṛṇu || 7.98.20 ||
translation: स therefore, त्वं you, पुरुषशार्दूल O best among men, धर्मेण with righteousness, सुसमाहितः well-composed/attentive. शेषं the remaining, भविष्यं future, काकुत्स्थ O Kakutstha, काव्यं poem, रामायणं Ramayana, शृणु listen.
explanation: Therefore, O best among men, O Kakutstha, being well-composed and attentive to righteousness, listen to the remaining future events of the Ramayana poem.

shloka_text: उत्तरं नाम काव्यस्य शेषमत्र महायशः । तच्छृणुष्व महातेज ऋषिभिः सार्धमुत्तमम् ।। 7.98.21 ।।
transliteration: uttaraṃ nāma kāvyasya śeṣamatra mahāyaśaḥ | tacchṛṇuṣva mahāteja ṛṣibhiḥ sārdhamuttamam || 7.98.21 ||
translation: उत्तरं Uttaram, नाम named, काव्यस्य of the epic poem, शेषम् the remainder, अत्र here, महायशः O greatly renowned one, तत् that, शृणुष्व listen, महातेज O greatly effulgent one, ऋषिभिः with the sages, सार्धम् together with, उत्तमम् excellent.
explanation: O greatly renowned and effulgent Rama, listen here to this excellent concluding part of the epic poem, named Uttara, along with the sages.

shloka_text: न खल्वन्येन काकुत्स्थ श्रोतव्यमिदमुत्तमम् । परमम् ऋषिणा वीर त्वयैव रघुनन्दन ।। 7.98.22 ।।
transliteration: na khalvanyena kākutstha śrotavyamidamuttamam | paramam ṛṣiṇā vīra tvayaiva raghunandana || 7.98.22 ||
translation: न not, खलु indeed, अन्येन by another, काकुत्स्थ O Kakutstha, श्रोतव्यम् to be heard, इदम् this, उत्तमम् excellent, परमम् supreme, ऋषिणा by the sage, वीर O hero, त्वया by you, एव only, रघुनन्दन O delight of the Raghus.
explanation: Indeed, O Kakutstha, O hero, O delight of the Raghus, this excellent and supreme work, composed by the sage, is not to be heard by anyone else, but only by you.

shloka_text: एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं ब्रह्मा त्रिभुवनेश्वरः । जगाम त्रिदिवं देवो देवैः सह सबान्धवैः ।। 7.98.23 ।।
transliteration: etāvaduktvā vacanaṃ brahmā tribhuvaneśvaraḥ | jagāma tridivaṃ devo devaiḥ saha sabāndhavaiḥ || 7.98.23 ||
translation: एतावत् thus much, उक्त्वा having said, वचनम् the word, ब्रह्मा Brahma, त्रिभुवनेश्वरः the lord of the three worlds, जगाम went, त्रिदिवम् to heaven, देवः the god, देवैः with the gods, सह together with, सबान्धवैः with his relatives.
explanation: Having spoken thus, Brahma, the lord of the three worlds, the god, went to heaven along with the other gods and his associates.

shloka_text: ये च तत्र महात्मान ऋषयो ब्राह्मलौकिकाः । ब्रह्मणा समनुज्ञाता न्यवर्तन्त महौजसः । उत्तरं श्रोतुमनसो भविष्यं यच्च राघवे ।। 7.98.24 ।।
transliteration: ye ca tatra mahātmāna ṛṣayo brāhmalaukikāḥ | brahmaṇā samanujñātā nyavartanta mahaujasaḥ | uttaraṃ śrotumanaso bhaviṣyaṃ yacca rāghave || 7.98.24 ||
translation: ये those who, च and, तत्र there, महात्मानः great-souled ones, ऋषयः sages, ब्राह्मलौकिकाः belonging to Brahma's world, ब्रह्मणा by Brahma, समनुज्ञाताः permitted, न्यवर्तन्त returned, महौजसः greatly powerful ones, उत्तरम् the Uttara Kanda, श्रोतुमनसः desirous to hear, भविष्यम् the future, यत् which, च and, राघवे regarding Rama.
explanation: And those great-souled, greatly powerful sages from Brahma's world, who were desirous to hear the Uttara Kanda and the future events concerning Rama, returned after being permitted by Brahma.

shloka_text: ततो रामः शुभां वाणीं देवदेवस्य भाषिताम् । श्रुत्वा परमतेजस्वी वाल्मीकिमिदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.98.25 ।।
transliteration: tato rāmaḥ śubhāṃ vāṇīṃ devadevasya bhāṣitām | śrutvā paramatejasvī vālmīkimidamabravīt || 7.98.25 ||
translation: ततः then, रामः Rama, शुभाम् auspicious, वाणीम् speech, देवदेवस्य of the god of gods, भाषिताम् spoken, श्रुत्वा having heard, परमतेजस्वी most effulgent, वाल्मीकिम् to Valmiki, इदम् this, अब्रवीत् said.
explanation: Then, the most effulgent Rama, having heard the auspicious words spoken by Brahma, the god of gods, said this to Valmiki.

shloka_text: भगवन् श्रोतुमनस ऋषयो ब्राह्मलौकिकाः । भविष्यदुत्तरं यन्मे श्वोभूते सम्प्रवर्तताम् ।। 7.98.26 ।।
transliteration: bhagavan śrotumanasa ṛṣayo brāhmalaukikāḥ | bhaviṣyaduttaraṃ yanme śvobhūte sampravartatām || 7.98.26 ||
translation: भगवन् O venerable one, श्रोतुमनसः desirous of hearing, ऋषयः sages, ब्राह्मलौकिकाः from Brahma's realm, भविष्यत् future, उत्तरम् latter part, यत् which, मे by me, श्वोभूते on the morrow, सम्प्रवर्तताम् let it be commenced.
explanation: Valmiki addresses the venerable sages from Brahma's realm, expressing his desire for the future, latter part of his Ramayana to be commenced on the following day for them to hear.

shloka_text: एवं विनिश्चयं कृत्वा सम्प्रगृह्य कुशीलवौ । तं जनौघं विसृज्याथ पर्णशालामुपागमत् । तामेव शोचतः सीतां सा व्यतीयाय शर्वरी ।। 7.98.27 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ viniścayaṃ kṛtvā sampragṛhya kuśīlavau | taṃ janaughaṃ visṛjyātha parṇaśālāmupāgamat | tāmeva śocataḥ sītāṃ sā vyatīyāya śarvarī || 7.98.27 ||
translation: एवम् thus, विनिश्चयम् decision, कृत्वा having made, सम्प्रगृह्य having taken, कुशीलवौ Kusha and Lava, तम् that, जनौघम् multitude of people, विसृज्य having dismissed, अथ then, पर्णशालाम् to the hermitage, उपागमत् he went, ताम् that, एव indeed, शोचतः lamenting, सीताम् for Sita, सा that, व्यतीयाय passed away, शर्वरी night.
explanation: Having made this decision and accepted Kusha and Lava, Rama dismissed the crowd and returned to his hermitage, where that night passed as he grieved for Sita. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे ऽष्टनवतितमः सर्गः ।। 98 ।। Thus ends the ninety-eighth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
